title: Cross-tenant audit correlator, attestation escrow and RBACv2 stabilization
author: Anika Rao
description:
Motivation: Customers running multi-tenant workloads asked for stronger cross-tenant audit correlation for incident investigations while still preserving tenant isolation guarantees. Separately, operator teams want an auditable KMS escrow path to support emergency decrypt workflows for regulated customers. This PR delivers a small, backwards-compatible RBACv2 stabilization pass plus a new audit correlator service and a lightweight KMS escrow attestation flow.

What this PR does: - Adds an audit correlator that augments existing audit events with stable correlation keys (hashed claim fingerprints + region pin) to make multi-service traces joinable without leaking tenant-identifying metadata. The correlator lives as a library and an optional sidecar to keep runtime opt-in. - Introduces a KMS escrow attestor component that records escrow requests to the audit log, ties them to an operator attestation token, and attaches sealed metadata so downstream auditors can validate the request timeline. No plaintext key material is stored. - Stabilizes several RBACv2 decision code paths: reduces decision cache jitter (deterministic key ordering), adds stricter deny-before-allow evaluation for operator-scoped bindings, and hardens temporal grants evaluation to respect region pinning flags. - Adds operator-facing docs and runbook (docs/operator/escrow-and-correlation.md) describing escalation, attestation token minting, and how audit proofs are validated during postmortems.

Implementation notes: - The correlator computes correlation_key = HMAC_SHA256(service_claims_fingerprint || region_pin || correlation_salt_v1) and emits correlation_key as an opaque hex string in audit metadata (field audit.corr_key). This design intentionally avoids tenant IDs or other PII. - KMS escrow attestor integrates with existing kms/allocator package via a new EscrowManager interface; the implementation only records a sealed envelope (kms.escrow.envelope_ref) in the audit log and submits a verified attestation record to the compliance indexer. - RBACv2: decision engine changes are limited to four functions in pkg/authz/rbacv2/engine.go and the in-memory cache eviction policy; the public API surface is unchanged. All new feature flags are behind feature gates: feature.audit_correlator and feature.kms_escrow.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for correlator hashing and envelope sealing - [x] Integration test that exercises a simulated operator escrow request and verifies audit envelope contents - [x] RBACv2 deterministic ordering tests - [x] Documentation and runbook added - [x] Feature gates added and defaulted to off for Dedicated and Private by config

Rollout plan: - Merge to main in squash, enable feature flags in canary clusters for a week, run the escrow e2e with compliance team, then enable correlation-only in hosted read-only telemetry pipelines, and only enable full escrow in Dedicated/Private with an operator onboarding checklist.

Backwards compatibility: Correlation key is optional metadata; existing consumers ignore unknown audit fields. Escrow attestation is guarded by feature gate and a tenant-level allowlist; no customer KMS operations change unless explicitly opted in via the operator runbook.

Security considerations: - Correlator design is reviewed with privacy and SRE: it never emits tenant identifiers and correlation_salt_v1 is derived per-deployment and rotated quarterly. - Escrow requests mandate operator attestation (MFA-backed) and are rate-limited; audit envelopes are signed with the service signing key. - RBAC changes intentionally shift deny-evaluation earlier; tests and a brief canary were run to ensure no regressions in common flows.

Follow-ups (future PRs planned): - telemetry consumer to index correlation_key for faster cross-service queries - administrative UI for escrow request lifecycle (approval/deny) - automated audit proof replay tool to validate escrow envelopes during DR scenarios

Related work: Linear: ENG-2104 (audit-correlator), SEC-987 (escrow-attestation); references: docs/arch/audit-design.md and pkg/kms/README.md.
